record.original_question: Let X be a T0 space. Call X a strong d-space if for every directed subset D of X, every point x in X, and every open set U, whenever the intersection of the sets up(d) intersect up(x) over all d in D is contained in U, there is already some d in D such that up(d) intersect up(x) is contained in U. If {X_i | i in I} is an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces, must the product space product_i X_i again be a strong d-space?

evidence.quote: Question 1.1. Is the product space of arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space?

A T0 space X is called a strong d-space if for any directed subset D of X, x in X and U in O(X), intersection over d in D of up d intersect up x subset U implies up d intersect up x subset U for some d in D.
In Section 3, we will give negative answers to Question 1.1 and Question 1.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a T0 topological space. For a point y ∈ X, let ↑y = {z ∈ X : y ≤ z} denote the upper set of y in the specialization order (where y ≤ z iff y belongs to the closure of {z}). Call X a strong d-space if for every directed subset D ⊆ X (directed with respect to the specialization order), every point x ∈ X, and every open set U ⊆ X, the condition
   ⋂_{d ∈ D} (↑d ∩ ↑x) ⊆ U
implies that there exists some d ∈ D such that ↑d ∩ ↑x ⊆ U.

Question: If {X_i : i ∈ I} is an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces, equipped with the product topology, must the product space ∏_{i ∈ I} X_i again be a strong d-space?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative: products of strong d-spaces need not be strong d-spaces. This is established in work on strong d-spaces by Xu, Shen, Xi, and Zhao (and related papers), where counterexamples are constructed.

status_evidence.title: On strong d-spaces (arXiv:2109.11299)
status_evidence.snippet: In Section 3, we will give negative answers to Question 1.1 and Question 1.2.
status_evidence.claim: The product of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces is shown not to be a strong d-space in general.
